matches.quote: The two runs from the same cooldown cover adjacent ranges, 12 to 20 mT and 20 to 30 mT, so no range was measured twice within one cooldown.
a step at 22.5 mT appears in both cooldowns (with 20.0 and 20.5 mT close by); how often would that happen if entry fields were random?
how did you decide that a step is one vortex, given that you also allow "one or a few flux quanta" (p. 4)?

notes: C8 vs P10: Referee C8 accepts the text's claim that jump fields differ across cooldowns and asks why they are not identical for the same device; P10 notices in Fig. 3 that steps at 22.5 mT and ~20 mT actually coincide across cooldowns and questions the random-entry claim. Both force the authors to address what governs step reproducibility across thermal cycles, so C8 is judged 'partly'. C10 vs P5: both target the ambiguity on p. 4-5 between 'one or a few flux quanta' and the single-vortex assumption, though C10 focuses on sparse spacing and multi-vortex vs multi-quantum vortices while P5 focuses on single-vortex stiffness extraction, so C10 is judged 'partly'. C3 vs P4/P8: P4 asks to plot the fitted flux offset phi_off vs B_ip to test for flux jumps in the SQUID arms rather than coil-alignment cross-coupling, so C3 is 'not raised'.
